title: Canonical geometrically reduced subscheme carrying separable points

source.place: Brian Conrad, Finiteness theorems for algebraic groups over function fields, Lemma 3.1.1, printed p.15 (PDF page 16), read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/cosetfinite.pdf. WANTED locally. The displayed lemma gives the general scheme construction, functoriality, products and separable base change; the geometrically reduced case follows from its uniqueness. No Stacks tag is claimed for the complete assertion.

proof.text: We first record the affine bookkeeping used below. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], a closed subscheme on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. It is finite type over $k$ when $A$ is: the images of a finite generating list still generate. Closed immersions are monomorphisms: a ring map out of $A/I$ is determined by its composite with the surjection $A\to A/I$, and these unique affine factorizations agree on overlaps. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], affine products and field base changes have rings $A\otimes_kB$ and $A\otimes_kK$, and these charts cover the fibre products. Tensoring quotient maps gives quotient maps, explicitly $(A/I)\otimes_k(B/J)=(A\otimes_kB)/(I\otimes B+A\otimes J)$ and $(A/I)\otimes_kK=(A\otimes_kK)/(I\otimes K)$. Thus products and field base changes of the closed subschemes below remain closed subschemes; their finite generating lists give finite type. Here the fibre-product maps and their identifications are always the ones characterized by [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tags 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines), 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product); affine quotient and tensor universal properties. Elementary affine bookkeeping.

proof.text: Choose a separable closure $k^s/k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], and put $T_X=X(k^s)$ and $C_X=\overline{\{\operatorname{image}(t):t\in T_X\}}\subseteq |X|$. Let $i_X:X^\natural\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $C_X$, provided by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is finite type by step 1. The family $T_X$ is stable under every $k$-automorphism of $k^s$, because composing a $k$-point with such an automorphism is again a $k$-point. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-point-closure-universal-density] with $Z=X$ and this whole family: the result is geometrically reduced. Its common-overfield qualification covers any field extension $E/k$: choose an algebraic closure of $E$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and embed $k^s$ into it by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] (an algebraically closed field is separably closed). This supplies exactly the common algebraically closed overfield in that node. Every $t\in T_X$ factors through $i_X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme], since a field spectrum is reduced and its image is in $C_X$. Uniqueness follows from the monomorphism in step 1.

source.place: Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction); geometric reducedness from the existing separable-point-closure node.

proof.text: Let $L/k$ be any separable extension in the stated, possibly transcendental sense, and $x:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$. Choose a finite-type affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing its image, and let $S\subseteq L$ be the image of $A\to L$. Then $S$ is a finite-type domain over $k$, and $F=\operatorname{Frac}S\subseteq L$ is finitely generated as a field. Every finitely generated subfield of $F/k$ is one of $L/k$, so $F/k$ is separable by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-generic-point-over-field] choose $0\ne g\in S$ with $S_g$ smooth over $k$. The affine comparison [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes $V=\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ a smooth $k$-scheme mapping to $U$, and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ factors through $V$ since $g$ is invertible in $L$. By [lem-pc-dense-separable-points], the closed $v\in V$ with $\kappa(v)/k$ finite separable are dense in $V$. Each embeds into $k^s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed], so its image in $X$ is the image of a point in $T_X$, hence belongs to $C_X$. The inverse image of $C_X$ in $V$ is closed and contains this dense set, hence is all of $V$. The ring $S_g$ is a subring of $L$ and therefore has no nonzero nilpotents; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff] makes $V$ reduced. Now [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $V\to X$ through $i_X$, and composition gives the desired factorization of $x$. It is unique by step 1. This proves $X^\natural(L)=X(L)$.

source.place: Tag 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point); morphisms.tex Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); varieties.tex Tag 056U (lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense); schemes.tex Tag 0356.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be another geometrically reduced closed subscheme with the asserted point equality. It is finite type by step 1. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian: its coordinate field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated. Thus [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $Z/k$ locally finitely presented. By [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open], its smooth locus is dense. On each smooth open in the definition of this locus, [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] gives dense closed points with finite separable residue fields. Embed each such field into $k^s$ using [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed]; their images in $X$ lie in $C_X$. Since $j^{-1}(C_X)$ is closed and contains a dense subset of every such open, and these opens have dense union, it is all of $Z$. Conversely every $k^s$-point of $X$ factors through $Z$ by the assumed point equality, so $|Z|$ is a closed subset containing $T_X$ and therefore $C_X$. We obtain $|Z|=C_X$. Both closed subschemes are reduced, so the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies their ideal sheaves and gives $Z=X^\natural$ as closed subschemes. This also removes dependence on the chosen $k^s$. If $X$ is itself geometrically reduced, the identity closed subscheme has the point equality, so this uniqueness gives $X^\natural=X$.

source.place: Tags 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open) and 056U; schemes.tex Tag 01J3, uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme.

proof.text:
Let $f:X	o Y$ be a $k$-morphism between finite-type schemes. Composition sends $T_X$ into $T_Y$. Continuity implies $f(C_X)\subseteq\overline{f(T_X)}\subseteq C_Y$: indeed the inverse image of the closed subset $C_Y$ is closed and contains $T_X$, hence its closure. The scheme $X^
atural$ is reduced, so [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives $f^
atural:X^
atural	o Y^
atural$ with $i_Yf^
atural=fi_X$. Step 1 makes this restriction unique. The identity of $X^
atural$ has the required equation for $f=\mathrm{id}_X$. For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow h Z$, the composite $h^
atural f^
atural$ has the equation required for $(hf)^
atural$; uniqueness gives equality. This proves functoriality.

source.place: Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction); continuity and uniqueness of factorization give the functor laws.

proof.text:
Put $P=X^
atural	imes_kY^
atural$, a closed finite-type subscheme of $X	imes_kY$ by step 1. It is geometrically reduced as follows. For every extension $E/k$, cover $X^
atural_E$ and $Y^
atural_E$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Their rings are geometrically reduced over $E$: after any further field extension these opens remain open in the corresponding reduced schemes, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff] translates this to rings. In particular $B$ is reduced. By [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-base-change] over the field $E$, $A\otimes_EB$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], and the same affine reducedness criterion, these rings give a reduced affine cover of $P_E$. Thus $P$ is geometrically reduced. For separable $L/k$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $P(L)=X^
atural(L)	imes Y^
atural(L)=X(L)	imes Y(L)=(X	imes_kY)(L)$ by step 3. Uniqueness in step 4 proves $P=(X	imes_kY)^
atural$. The nullary product is $\operatorname{Spec}k$: every field base change is a field spectrum and hence reduced, so step 4 gives its core equal to itself. Induction gives compatibility with every finite product; the identifications respect projections by their defining universal properties.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change); schemes.tex Tags 01J2, 01JQ, 01JR; affine tensor calculation and the defining fibre-product universal property.

proof.text:
Let $K/k$ be separable and $Q=(X^
atural)_K\hookrightarrow X_K$. This is a finite-type closed subscheme by step 1. It is geometrically reduced over $K$: for every $E/K$, the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Q_E$ with $X^
atural_E$, which is reduced by step 2. If $L/K$ is separable, [lem-sfb-separable-field-extension-transitivity] says that $L/k$ is separable as well; this node explicitly permits transcendental extensions. A $K$-point $\operatorname{Spec}L	o X_K$ corresponds to its $k$-map $\operatorname{Spec}L	o X$ together with the fixed map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Step 3 gives a unique factorization of that $k$-map through $X^
atural$; pairing this factorization with the same fixed map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ gives a unique point of $Q(L)$, by the fibre-product universal property. Therefore $Q(L)=X_K(L)$ for every separable $L/K$. Applying step 4 with ground field $K$ yields $(X^
atural)_K=(X_K)^
atural$ as closed subschemes. This argument uses separability, not commutation of ordinary reduction with an arbitrary field extension.

source.place: Tags 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness) and 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions), through the existing general transitivity node; scheme part is the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text:
Finally let $X=G$ be an affine finite-type group scheme. Apply step 5 to its multiplication, inverse and identity maps of [def-sc-group-scheme]. By step 6 their source cores are respectively $G^
atural	imes_kG^
atural$, $G^
atural$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus these maps give multiplication $m^
atural$, inverse $a^
atural$ and identity $e^
atural$ on $G^
atural$, and $i_G$ commutes with each operation. To verify associativity, compose the two maps from $(G^
atural)^3$ with $i_G$: both are the restriction of the associative multiplication on $G$. The monomorphism in step 1 cancels $i_G$, so the two maps agree. The same cancellation proves both unit equations and both inverse equations. These are precisely the group diagrams. For every $k$-algebra $R$, step 1 makes $G^
atural(R)	o G(R)$ injective, and the three operation equations say its image contains the identity and is closed under multiplication and inverse, so it is a subgroup. This is a closed subgroup scheme in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and it is geometrically reduced by step 2. The quotient description in step 1 also makes it affine. If $X$ is empty then $T_X=C_X=\varnothing$ and the construction gives the empty closed subscheme; all preceding point, uniqueness, product and base-change assertions still apply.

source.place: Group-object diagrams and the definition of a closed subgroup scheme; restrictions supplied by steps 5-6.

split_report.summary: Q158 retained the statement and its statement dependencies, supplied eight explicit steps using existing nodes only, and searched the project library plus Mathlib with two semantic phrasings, Loogle and source grep. The construction is the reduced closure of all k^s-points. Generic smoothness of the coordinate-image algebra proves the point property for every separable extension, including transcendental ones. Dense smooth opens prove uniqueness; tensor reducedness gives products; general separability transitivity gives base change; the group diagrams are checked after composing with the closed monomorphism. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: This created node has blueprint ancestor None, as blueprint_refs.py ancestor reports. The inherited specified from.place and via chain are retained. The current latest sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability unit and direct-images proof (3) were read: this is a general scheme prerequisite in the retained alteration/unipotent-group branch, not a change to a unit route. Steps 1-4 realize the inherited separable-point core prerequisite; steps 5-8 prove its functorial, product, base-change and subgroup clauses. Searches for geometrically reduced, separable points, separable extension and reduced closed subscheme found no blueprint node stating the complete item.

tool_uses.why: Step 3 uses the finite-type domain generic-smoothness criterion to realize a separable-valued point through a smooth affine source; this unit has no such algebra lemma.
Step 3 converts the smooth algebra supplied by the generic-point criterion into a smooth affine scheme for the density theorem.
Steps 2, 3 and 5 use the general reduced-source closed-factorization criterion; this is a scheme-theoretic tool, not a replacement of a unit step.
Step 6 uses only the general commutative-algebra tensor-reducedness theorem over a field (Stacks 034N) to prove reducedness of product charts; no trace-formula assertion is used.

Geometric reducedness comes from lem-sfb-separable-point-closure-universal-density; its common-overfield restriction is handled by choosing an algebraic closure Ω of E and embedding k^s in it. Step 3 proves the point property for any separable L, including transcendental L, via generic smoothness of the coordinate image (07ND node) and density of separable points (056U). Step 4 proves uniqueness using the dense smooth locus (056V node, lfp via the locally Noetherian base) and clause (3) of the reduced-induced node. Steps 5-8 (functoriality, products via 034N, separable base change via the transitivity node, closed subgroup by cancelling the monomorphism) are correct, and steps 1 and 8 are genuinely elementary. Small cases checked: inseparable point Spec k[x]/(x^p-a) gives an empty core, α_p gives the identity point, and the empty scheme works. Stacks 034N, 056V and 07ND were read in the local tex. lean.note: The declarations together render every clause. Canonical helpers construct the reduced induced closure of the separable-closure points using Mathlib vanishingIdeal/subscheme.
